input: Recent findings suggest that direct KRAS G12D inhibition may improve treatment response in pancreatic cancer.
Combining KRAS G12D inhibition with chemotherapy may delay relapse compared with either treatment alone in pancreatic cancer.
BCL-xL degradation and mTOR inhibition may sensitize pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to KRAS G12D inhibitors.
CRBN-based KRAS G12D degraders may produce durable target depletion and tumor regression in pancreatic cancer models.
Farnesyl-transferase inhibition may overcome resistance to KRAS G12D targeting in pancreatic cancer.
The apparent response to KRAS G12D inhibition can differ between two-dimensional and three-dimensional pancreatic cancer models.
Chitosan-PEG nanoparticles may improve co-delivery of paclitaxel and KRAS G12D-directed siRNA to pancreatic cancer cells.
Multiple genetic and transcriptional programs can drive acquired resistance to KRAS inhibition in pancreatic cancer.
Pancreatic cancer cell state may influence response to KRAS G12D inhibition.
Claims about KRAS G12D therapies in pancreatic cancer should distinguish preclinical efficacy from established patient outcomes.
